newsitem.title: UK: American holds cargo fuel surcharges.
newsitem.headline: American holds cargo fuel surcharges.

text.p: American Airlines is to continue imposing cargo fuel surcharges on its customers until further notice, its managing director-international cargo sales John Smith told Reuters.
He said this was despite the lifting of similar surcharges by rival transatlatic carriers Delta Air Lines (effective March 13), Virgin Atlantic (April 1) and United (April 7).

"Our latest information is that our fuel prices are still 22 percent higher than they were at this time last year. Obviously we will keep a close eye on the situation but we are keeping the surcharge for the time being," he said.
Smith added that American imposed an international systemwide fuel-related surcharge of about 10 percent on cargo rates -- six pence per kg in the UK -- on November 15 last year.
"We watched as fuel prices went up and up but we did not act to impose surcharges until some two weeks after many other airlines," he noted.

"Our decision to hold the surcharge is based on our costings. While we obviously will aim to be competitive, we need to make similar (profit) margins to those we earned before (fuel prices went up)," he added.
Smith said that by abolishing its cargo surcharges, arch-rival United would win "some traffic they otherwise might not get", but he said this would not influence his carrier's policy.
"We followed two weks after the others with surcharges and we will probably be two weeks longer in lifting them," he stated.
Meanwhile, Air Canada said it had decided to retain its own cargo fuel surcharges until further notice.
